This bill would abolish the Australian Astronomical Observatory and move its scientific roles to outside organisations.
The government would transfer telescope operations to a university consortium and move instrumentation work to a group of universities.
The Anglo-Australian Telescope would operate until at least 2024-25, five years longer than previously planned.
Abolishes the Australian Astronomical Observatory and its governance structures from 1 July 2018.
Transfers the Anglo-Australian Telescope's operations to the Australian National University on behalf of a consortium managed by Australia Astronomy Limited.
Transfers the AAO's instrumentation capability to a consortium of Macquarie University, the Australian National University and the University of Sydney.
Amends and renames the Australian Astronomical Observatory Act 2010.
Repeals the Australian Astronomical Observatory (Transitional Provisions) Act 2010.

The Australian Astronomical Observatory, its staff, the Department of Industry, Innovation and Science, the Australian National University, Macquarie University, the University of Sydney, Australia Astronomy Limited, and the Australian astronomy community.

The bill supports the government's 2017-18 budget measure to transition Australia's optical astronomy capability, including transferring the Australian Astronomical Observatory's operations, assets and staff to university-led consortia. The government has entered a 10-year Strategic Partnership with the European Southern Observatory, the Australian National University will lead a consortium to operate the Anglo-Australian Telescope until the mid-2020s, and Macquarie University will develop a national optical instrumentation capability.

Labor reluctantly supports the Australian Astronomical Observatory (Transition) Bill 2018 to prevent the closure of the Anglo-Australian Telescope and AAO laboratories in 2020, but criticises the government for offloading costs to universities, resulting in the loss of 4–5 jobs at the telescope and up to nine at the North Ryde instrumentation labs, while saving $26.1 million over the forward estimates.

The speaker reluctantly supported the bill to abolish the Australian Astronomical Observatory and transfer its operations—the Anglo-Australian Telescope to a consortium led by ANU and the instrumentation capability to a consortium led by Macquarie University—as part of a $119.2 million strategic partnership with the European Southern Observatory, but criticised the government for offloading costs onto financially strained universities and for causing 13–14 job losses.

The bill transitions the Australian Astronomical Observatory’s operations to the research sector from 1 July 2018, giving effect to a 10‑year strategic partnership with the European Southern Observatory (ESO) that began on 11 July 2017. The Anglo‑Australian Telescope will transfer to an Australian National University‑led consortium, and the observatory’s instrumentation capability will transfer to a consortium led by Macquarie University.
